Varamhar (F42)

Survey region: Bulwar.

One-sentence positioning: Turn a small Sun Elf kingdom pressed by stronger neighbours into a centre of magical research, then try to manufacture a god with your own hands.

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 74/100｜Autocracy 82/100｜Magic↔Artifice 98/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 98/100)｜Pluralism 35/100.

The v2.1 value score is Neutral (53/100), with a mixed trajectory.

Story: high｜Mission-tree length: medium (24 dedicated missions)｜Mission-tree update: base mod v1.37.5.0, adapted to the current magic scripts｜Distinctiveness: very high｜Grind: high｜Early pressure: high｜Expansion capacity: medium-high.

A Young Kingdom, Ancient Magic

Varamhar is an existing Sun Elf kingdom in 1444. It uses the Phoenix Estate reform (script key phoenix_akalate), follows the Bulwari Sun Cult and accepts Zanite culture. Karodir I Varamzuir has ruled since 1375 and is a powerful mage with a scholarly character. The country history also establishes mage organisations and magical development, so the opening advantage is not a large territory but magical power that can be mobilised immediately.【Local history script】

The offline English Wiki describes it as a comparatively late Sun Elf successor state after the collapse of the Phoenix Empire. At the end of the Second Cinder War, Galindil founded the kingdom in 1272; it was squeezed by Harpies and other Sun Elf powers, remained small, yet became known for its magical tradition. The earlier people and dynastic history are background only and cannot replace the current opening ruler with Wiki figures.【Wiki material】

The Academy is another case where the date boundary matters. The Wiki records Karodir founding the famous academy in 1446, after the game starts; the local missions instead treat the academy as a future objective requiring investment and construction. Thus the 1444 country has mages and a research tradition, but it has not already completed the academy, divine research and apotheosis project.【Wiki material】【Local script】

Turning the Country into a Laboratory

The 24 dedicated missions first require Varamhar to deal with the northern threat and open room for development, then connect research, religion and material management. The war against the Harpies is presented in the narrative as restoring security and trade; that is the country's own justification for its external action, not an objective endorsement of every method.【Local script】【Local flavour text】

Building the academy requires money and all three monarch-point types, then combines with universities, mage towers, mage-estate support and suitable organisations. What changes the feel of the campaign is turning magic from an individual ruler's ability into a national project: the player cannot simply wait for a mage to grow naturally, but must align the economy, estates, buildings and research conditions.【Local script】

The other side of the divine project is resources. Precursor relics, glass, porcelain and wine feed elemental storage, concentrated sunlight and the refining of divine magic. Trade and production are not side activities here; they are the conditions that keep the laboratory operating. The religious route also requires winning over priests and adjusting the relationship between the country and its orders, showing that manufacturing a god cannot be detached from the legitimacy structure of the Sun Cult.【Local script】

That is why Varamhar's story is unlike that of an ordinary magical great power: a small successor kingdom must combine an academy, trade goods, religious institutions and its ruler into a power beyond the mortal. Magic is not a free resource that wins the game when clicked; it is a long-term project that continually pushes the country toward another threshold.

Divinity Is Not a Cost-Free Reward

The experiments cause concrete damage. A representative event adds severe devastation in province 609, reducing its tax, production and manpower base and lowering national stability. These are local losses directly recorded in the current script; they cannot be softened into “research sacrifice”, nor can one manpower penalty be used to infer a scale of living sacrifice that the text does not establish.【Local script】

The final apotheosis event is divided into tiers by research count. Different preparations produce different ruler outcomes; one tier directly ends the original ruler's life before entering the apotheosis narrative, while a higher tier also includes an effect that disables necromancy. The complete branch has not been audited as a guide, so this article does not promise that one fixed sequence always produces the strongest immortal ruler. What can be established is that the country's future revolves around god-making and ruler transformation, not a risk-free automatic victory route.【Local script】

Varamhar can form the Phoenix Empire through an eligible decision. Its mission potential conditions specifically allow F38 or F97 countries that were formerly F42 to retain this route, so formation does not immediately erase the country's god-making story. Nor can Varamhar be written as the Phoenix Empire already existing in 1444.【Local script】

Playstyle and Personality

Start by using the opening mage to stabilise the military and economy, then advance the academy, buildings, estates and trade resources together; later play focuses on the ruler, research conditions and the divine project rather than simply taking more provinces. Preparation order, the ruler's lifespan and material thresholds are the main sources of grind. Older player posts emphasise early pressure, while discussions of the new magic system debate attribute spells and immortality events; their old numbers are not current-version instructions.【Community opinion】

The provisional personality profile is Expansion 74 / Autocracy 82 / Magic–Artifice 98 (intensity 98) / Pluralism 35. The value score is Neutral 53, with a mixed trajectory: the academy and public development provide real benefits, while experimental losses and power goals pursued “at any cost” limit restraint. Confirmed devastation does not prove every allegation of treating the population as a resource, so medium confidence is retained.

Recommended for players who enjoy mage rulers, research projects and apotheosis narratives. Players who dislike multiple prerequisites, ruler-survival risks and experimental costs should avoid it. Historical, formation and ending boundaries are recorded in the evidence record.

National ideas (reference appendix)

Native English national-idea names and descriptions are reproduced below with the inherited effect displays. Traditions apply when this set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Alternative sets and successor ideas do not automatically stack. Descriptions may recount history or depict future ideals, not events already completed in 1444. Native English wording is reused rather than back-translating embellished Chinese localisation. Inherited display-unit assumptions remain unverified; this translation does not correct source data.

Varamhar (F42) — Varamhari Ideas

Applicable condition; separate alternative, not a stacked set:

    trigger = {
        tag = F42
    }

Traditions: Varamhari Traditions

Effects: Shock damage: +10%; Diplomatic relations: +1.

Idea 1: The Varamhar Academy

The House of Knowledge of the Magical Arts, commonly known as the University of Ulmiš Idiqlat, was founded in 1446 by Karodir I Varamzuir, and quickly became the primary center of learning and study of magic in Bulwar. The university gained massive popularity when the king revoked the ban on human magi in his kingdom after the death of Taelarios of Irrliam, tripling the amount of magi of the institution.

During the Jadd Empire, Ulmiš Idiqlat remained an important and prestigious site even after the founding of other universities such as those in Brasan, Medurubar, and Jaddanzar during the Magi Renaissance. It opened education to all; however, it offered the widest array of courses to those who focus on the Sun Elf scholarly magic, and the Bulwari magic of Order.

Under the Divine-herald Tezalindor the Kind, the university became the first secular institution enabled to teach the Bulwari magic of Light, something that Karodir aimed for when he established it, training a new generation of Exorcist-priests who relied on arcane magic rather than divine.

Effects: Possible advisors: +1; Ruler culture advisor cost: -15%.

Idea 2: White Phoenix Guard

After the Great Assembly of Bulwar, King Daryam of Gišhuram gave a plot of land to Varamar, a distinguished captain of the Phoenix Legions, who founded the city of Varamhar alongside his subordinates.

Since its foundation, and especially during the war against Harpylen and later after the fall of the Jexisian Empire, Varamhar has had to deal with harpy raids and incursions. So Varamar had a special unit trained, the White Phoenix Guard, who were made up of highly mobile troops that would be able to swiftly respond to the threats of harpies and could quickly be deployed for defense or aid.

Effects: Movement speed: +15%.

Idea 3: Obligatory Internships

One of the benefits of having a university tied to your government is the access to a large pool of fresh talent. And both Varamhar and the Jadd Empire eagerly made use of that. Karodir instituted, and the Jadd Empire maintained, an obligatory internship period in government offices for all who attended the Academy. Magi were prized. Many of them aided the government in its daily tasks, while the most talented were offered military posts or moved on to secret projects.

Effects: All power costs: -2.5%.

Idea 4: Jaherian Sunlight

One of the great delicacies of Bulwar is Jaherian Sunlight. It is a sweet white wine made of raisins long-fermented in the sun. There are but a few locations throughout Bulwar where it is bottled, and its rarity has made it highly prized among the Cannorian upper class. However, the highest quality wine is made in Varamhar, and getting hold of a bottle of Varamhar Jaherian Sunlight is a clear sign of status.

Effects: Prestige: +1.

Idea 5: The Weakest Kingdom

After the fall of the Jexisian Empire, Bulwar divided itself among the local elven governors. Some thrived and drew powers to themselves while others shattered like the Kingdom of Dalarand during the Second Cinder War. Within this chaos, Kelindil Varamzuir, right hand of the king of Dalarand, plotted against his king with the Twelve of Bulwar to assassinate him. The plot was successful, and Kelindil carved his kingdom of Dalarand at the end of the war. His successors also learned to deal with the deck they were given, relying not on military might but on subterfuge to retain their independence as the weakest kingdom of the Suran Plain.

Effects: Spy network construction: +20%.

Idea 6: Bazaar Cities

Harpy raids had historically been a nightmare for merchants traveling through Bulwar, especially close to the Hills. In antiquity, the kingdom of Gišhuram responded with a program of construction: roofed cities to protect against harpy raids.

Many of those protections were in disrepair when Varamhar was established, but the rising menace of Ayarallen forced the Varamhari crown to restore the roof protections to their former glory. In exchange, they gained the love of the populace and a reputation of reliance among merchants, as they were much more eager to trade in a location where they or their goods did not just suddenly get carried away by an unexpected flock of harpies.

But Karodir not only repaired the existing Bazaar cities but improved them. Gišhuram, the city of astrologers and Varamhar’s capital, was protected with a roof composed of enchanted bronze tiles that could be retracted using magic. This allowed to increase the defensiveness of Varamhar’s capital while at the same time allowing the citizens to keep the view of the night sky from the city streets.

Effects: Domestic trade power: +10%.

Idea 7: Erdmagi

Unlike other Sun Elves who prefer close-combat spells, the Erdmagi are Varamhari magi specialized in powerful long-distance spells, a combination of Sun Elven traditions and the Bulwari magic of Order. These spells are costly and difficult to apply on the battlefields of the Suran Plain, where cavalry is king, but they are especially effective against stationary targets, such as walls, and slow-moving targets like siege engines or disciplined enemy formations.

During the siege of Gišhuram by the Desert Legion, the Erdmagi managed to keep the enemy at bay despite the city being attacked by both sides of the Buranun. Resisting the siege for over a year, the city surrendered after the death of Araš of Akalšes, when Karodir was released from the dungeons of Arašbar and was allowed to go into exile in exchange for his kingdom.

While some of the Erdmagi followed Karodir and joined the Jaherian Exemplars, most of them remained and joined the ranks of the nascent Jadd Empire, being renowned for their participation in the wars in Rahen against the Command.

Effects: Siege ability: +15%.

Ambition: Varamhari Ambition

Effects: Leader siege: +1.

Phoenix Empire (F38) — Phoenix Empire Ideas

Applicable condition; separate alternative, not a stacked set:

    trigger = {
        OR = {
            tag = F38
            tag = F97
        }
    }

Traditions: Phoenix Empire Traditions

Effects: Discipline: +5%; Core-creation cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Mantle of the Conqueror

"The conqueror stood at the world far edge and stared across the sunlit sea, And felt aught but crushing darkness, No thrill of victory. His blood sang for conquest but the world had struck him lame, And he wept great tears of fire and in thundering voice proclaimed. "I have reached my zenith, the highest I shall mark, For there are no more worlds to conquer, my soul is torn apart." He turned to face his empire, resigned to his fate, Jaher's time had passed, his death he did await. Till one takes up the mantle. The Phoenix Crown awaits." -from the Litany of Jaher by Sarada Razumir

Effects: Prestige: +1; Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3; Horde unity: +1.

Idea 2: The Order of the Light of Truth

The Sun Elves have long been styled the Chosen of Surael, destined to pave the way for his glorious return. Yet even as the Empire rose from the ashes of Jexis' reign there was a significant minority within its borders who refused to follow the true faith, not to mention those outside the Empire who still clung to dead gods. To combat this the priests of Surael formed The Order of the Light of Truth to spread the teachings of the Sun Temple to the farthest corners of the world, a task they proved apt in achieving.

Effects: Missionary strength: +3%.

Idea 3: The Empire of Palaces and Temples

The Phoenix Empire is one of soaring temples and palaces that reach towards the heavens, from the Palace of Eternal Fire to the Dawn temple its lands are filled with wonders undreamed, draped in marble and gold. It is not uncommon for the Elvish nobility to have sprawling estates larger than most towns as they add grander and grander edifices as the centuries wear on. With its resurgence the new Emperors undertook great projects to craft edifices to surpass anything found in the kingdoms of man and cement the glory of a new age of Elven leadership and peace.

Effects: Development cost: -5%; Construction cost: -10%.

Idea 4: From Ashes, the Phoenix Legion rises

In years past Jaher and Jexis lead the finest armies that the world has ever seen in their conquests. Legends of endless ranks of Legionaries clad in glittering golden armour and armed with shining silver blades are told across all of Cannor. Since the fall of Jexis the proud warrior traditions of the Phoenix Legions has faded into history and no more golden warriors march across Sarhal for the glory of the Sun Elf people.

Now that our great Empire has been reformed from the ashes, so too must the Legions march. For too long have those blades of legend been left to rust and dull under the weight of years. Once more the Phoenix Legions shall rise and once more the enemies of the Sun Elves shall tremble at their passing.

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +20%.

Idea 5: The Offices of Trade

Trade is one of the most vital practices in the Empire, much of the Elves' vast wealth is drawn from eastern goods traveling along the Empire's trade routes to be sold in the western lands of Cannor. To facilitate this trade, as well as to give an edge to their own merchant class, the Imperial government set about establishing a series of way stations called The Offices of Trade throughout its vast holdings where their merchants could rest and prepare for long journeys.

Effects: Trade efficiency: +10%; Movement speed: +15%.

Idea 6: The Gilded Menagerie

In the imperial capital of Bulwar, near to the Imperial Palace, lies a vast and sprawling complex of gold and lapis lazuli. Its official name is the Imperial Academy of Progress but most know it by another name The Gilded Menagerie. It is here that the future governors of the Empire are trained, many a noble house has sent its scions here in order to gain favour and position within the Imperial Bureaucracy. Its darker purpose is the training ground of the Empire's vast network of spies and assassins. It is said that in every court in Cannor, in every gathering of mages the Menagerie has a dozen sets of ears listening to every word and a dozen sharpened knives at every back.

Effects: Spy network construction: +25%; Advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 7: United under the Chosen People

The Phoenix Empire and its Sun Elf rulers are masters over vast and diverse lands stretching from horizon to horizon. It is within this Empire more than any other that cultures meet, trade and mingle under the enlightened rule of the chosen. The Sun Elves have accepted their destiny as those who will one day lead the entire world under their glorious rule and accept all the lesser races and accept all into the fold, provided they kneel at the feet of their betters.

Effects: Governing Capacity Modifier: +15%.

Ambition: Phoenix Empire Ambition

Effects: Administrative efficiency: +5%.
